candidates.exact_span: All bulk sewage sludge that is applied to agricultural land, forest, a public contact site, or a reclamation site shall be treated by one of the following alternatives 1 through 10 for Vector Attraction Reduction. If bulk sewage sludge is applied to a home garden, or bagged sewage sludge is applied to the land, only alternative 1 through alternative 8 shall be used.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is bulk versus bagged and the land-application site type determines which vector-attraction treatment alternatives are applicable; misclassification changes which monitoring/treatment obligations apply and whether missing evidence for alternatives 9–10 is relevant.

candidates.exact_span: The mass of volatile solids in the sewage sludge shall be reduced by a minimum of 38%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 1 sets an enforceable numeric volatile-solids-reduction threshold; a different reading of the reduction calculation or baseline could change whether a reported measurement exceeds the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: If Alternative 1 cannot be met for an anaerobically digested sludge, demonstration can be made by digesting a portion of the previously digested sludge anaerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 40 additional days at a temperature between 30 and 37 degrees Celsius. Volatile solids must be reduced by less than 17% to demonstrate compliance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This conditional bench-scale demonstration path applies only when Alternative 1 cannot be met for anaerobically digested sludge; interpretation of digester type, test duration, temperature range, and the <17% volatile-solids criterion changes which limit applies, whether bench-scale monitoring was required, and how missing primary-path data is classified.

candidates.exact_span: If Alternative 1 cannot be met for an aerobically digested sludge, demonstration can be made by digesting a portion of the previously digested sludge with a percent solid of 2% or less aerobically in the laboratory in a bench-scale unit for 30 additional days at 20 degrees Celsius. Volatile solids must be reduced by less than 15% to demonstrate compliance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This aerobic fallback path hinges on sludge solids concentration (2% or less), test length, temperature, and the <15% volatile-solids threshold; different interpretations change the applicable numeric limit, whether laboratory demonstration monitoring was obligatory, and the semantics of absent Alternative 1 results.

candidates.exact_span: The specific oxygen uptake rate (SOUR) for sewage sludge treated in an aerobic process shall be equal to or less than 1.5 milligrams of oxygen per hour per gram of total solids (dry weight basis) at a temperature of 20 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 4 imposes a numeric SOUR ceiling and specifies dry-weight and 20 °C measurement conditions; interpretation of units, solids basis, or temperature correction could change limit applicability and whether SOUR monitoring was required for aerobic-process sludge.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be treated in an aerobic process for 14 days or longer. During that time, the temperature of the sewage sludge shall be higher than 40 degrees Celsius and the average temperature of the sewage sludge shall be higher than 45 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 5 ties compliance to minimum treatment duration and simultaneous minimum instantaneous and average temperature thresholds; different readings of treatment period, temperature averaging, or what counts as the aerobic process window change both numeric compliance comparisons and temperature-monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: The pH of sewage sludge shall be raised to 12 or higher by alkali addition and, without the addition of more alkali shall remain at 12 or higher for two hours and then at 11.5 or higher for an additional 22 hours at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed; at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or given away in a bag or other container.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 6 combines staged pH limits with timing tied to use/disposal or bagging events; interpretation of when the clock starts, whether re-alkali addition resets compliance, and which trigger applies changes numeric limit comparisons, event-based monitoring requirements, and classification of missing pH records.

candidates.exact_span: The percent solids of sewage sludge that does not contain unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process shall be equal to or greater than 75 % based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials. Unstabilized solids are defined as organic materials in sewage sludge that have not been treated in either an aerobic or anaerobic treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 7 applies only to sludge without primary-process unstabilized solids and measures ≥75% solids before mixing; disputes over unstabilized-solid status, pre-mixing measurement timing, or solids calculation method change limit applicability, solids-monitoring obligations, and how absent data is resolved.

candidates.exact_span: Animals shall not be allowed to graze on the land for 30 days after application of sewage sludge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This post-application restriction creates a time-bounded operational obligation after sludge application; interpretation of application date or what constitutes grazing land affects whether the 30-day monitoring/restriction period was applicable in a given period.

candidates.exact_span: Turf grown on land where sewage sludge is applied shall not be harvested for 1 year after application of the sewage sludge when the harvested turf is placed on either land with a high potential for public exposure or a lawn, unless otherwise specified by the permitting authority.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Harvest prohibition depends on turf end-use (high-exposure land or lawn) and may be modified by the permitting authority; different readings of those conditions or authority specifications change whether the 1-year restriction was required and whether missing evidence should be treated as unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: Public access to land with a high potential for public exposure shall be restricted for 1 year after application of sewage sludge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability hinges on classifying land as high potential for public exposure and on the sludge application date; interpretation of exposure potential or timing changes whether the 1-year access-restriction obligation applied.

candidates.exact_span: Public access to land with a low potential for public exposure shall be restricted for 30 days after application of sewage sludge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 30-day restriction applies only where land is classified as low potential for public exposure; misclassification relative to the 1-year high-exposure rule changes which post-application access obligation was in force.
